readme.summary: Continuous, physically based model of the Sligo Creek watershed (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, Maryland, and Takoma Park, DC) from its headwaters to the Northwest Branch of the Anacostia River, calibrated to USGS flow and stage at Sligo Creek near Takoma Park (01650800). It has 27 urban hydrologic response units with three soil layers, regional and near-stream groundwater, compound channels and the Wheaton Branch stormwater pond, and is built in OpenHydroQual. This is the model behind the live digital twin; the parameter values written in are the calibrated (Levenberg-Marquardt) set the twin's main line uses. Forcing in this package: NOAA AORC hourly precipitation and gridMET reference evapotranspiration, October 2013 to September 2025 (the live twin uses MRMS radar rainfall scaled by 1.165).
readme.units:
- Time: days since 1899-12-30 00:00 UTC (the spreadsheet serial date; 45931.0 = 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC; the run starts at 41548.0 = 2013-10-01).
- SI units throughout: lengths and elevations in m (elevations NAVD88), areas in m², flows in m³/day, hydraulic conductivities in m/day, volumes in m³.
- `forcing/precip_scNN.csv`: `t_start,t_end,depth` with the precipitation depth in m over the interval (wet hours only; gaps are zero). `forcing/et_scNN.csv`: `t,rate` daily reference ET in m/day (gridMET ASCE short grass); the model scales it by the crop coefficients `corr_fact`.
- `observations/<site>_flow.csv`: `t,flow` in m³/day; `<site>_stage.csv`: `t,depth` in m above the zero-flow gage height (USGS gage height minus `gzf_fit_m` in the `gage_section_fits` table). Hourly in storm events, daily means otherwise.
- Coordinates: the GeoPackage layers keep the CRS of the source data (WGS84 longitude/latitude).
readme.run:
1. Install OpenHydroQual (https://github.com/ArashMassoudieh/OpenHydroQual).
2. Unzip this package and keep the folder structure (the model file refers to `templates/`, `forcing/` and `observations/` by relative paths). If a template is not found next to the model, OpenHydroQual falls back to its own template folder; use the copies supplied here, since the model depends on `riparian_urban_hru.json` and `compound_channel.json` as included.
3. Open `SligoCreek_model.ohq` in the OpenHydroQual GUI and run it, or use the console: `OpenHydroQual-Console SligoCreek_model.ohq -w <output folder>`.
4. Outputs go to `output.txt` (all state variables) and `observed_output.txt` (the modelled values at the observation points, with fit statistics printed at the end of the run). The twelve-year run with the interpreter takes a long time; shorten `simulation_end_time` at the top of the model file for a first test.
